name: The Twelve-Concept Interval Has an Octahedral Support Sphere
statement: For the twelve-concept trapped interval, the acquired supports are the twelve triples on $Y_0=\{1,2,3,4,9,10\}$ containing one of the disjoint pairs $P_1=\{1,2\}$, $P_2=\{3,4\}$, or $P_3=\{9,10\}$. The complementary pure rank-three complex is $\partial2^{P_1}*\partial2^{P_2}*\partial2^{P_3}\cong S^2$, the octahedral sphere. Its opposite vertex pairs are exactly the direction pairs of the three vertex-disjoint residual squares.
proof: Decoding the twelve support masks gives exactly four triples through each pair $P_i$, with no triple containing two pairs. A triple avoids all three pairs exactly when it chooses one coordinate from each pair, producing the eight facets of the join of three zero-spheres. The independently reconstructed residual graph has three vertex-disjoint squares with directions $P_1,P_2,P_3$.
